test: Build customer-year panel 2016-2024: active in year Y (>=1 order), lapsed = 0 orders in Y+1. Per customer-year compute short-line share (short lines / all lines) and return count (erp_returns joined to orders of that year). Band short share and returns; compare lapse rates within strata of branch x trade x order-volume band (logistic-style comparison via stratified differences / pooled within-stratum). Check whether lapsed customers come back later, whether another account with same name+branch stays active (identity), size of lapsers, and order frequency trend in the months before lapse. Size avoidable part as excess lapse attributable to high-short/return bands times their prior-year margin.
support: Lapse rate rises monotonically with short share or returns within branch/trade/size strata, by a material amount (e.g. several points) with adequate denominators, consistent across years; lapsers' orders decline before stopping; lapsers are not mostly tiny or duplicates.
weaken: Lapse rate flat (or falling) across short/return bands once order volume is held constant; lapse concentrated in small accounts (1-3 orders); many lapsed accounts reappear later or have a same-name same-branch sibling active next year.
expect: Raw lapse rate will look higher for high-short-share customers mainly because small customers have noisy shares and lapse more; returns will correlate positively with volume and so negatively with lapse raw. After controlling for volume I expect little or no effect (data looks synthetic and service-related fields are near-uniform). Moderate-strong expectation the hypothesis does not hold; ~65%.
